claims.text: Mechanical-property differences are not governed simply by the number of alloy constituents.
The property differences are governed by an interplay between deformation-induced nanotwinning and a magnetically tunable fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Magnetic frustration associated with Mn suppresses or eliminates a clear fcc-hcp energy difference in CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn-associated magnetic frustration limits development of a transformation-enhanced twin network.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi has less magnetic frustration and an energetically favored hcp state that promotes deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
Deformed CrCoNi contains nanoscale hcp regions.
The nanoscale hcp regions specifically form at twin or dislocation boundaries.
A combined twin-hcp nanostructure impedes dislocation motion more effectively.
Twinning can strengthen a material by impeding dislocations while multiple twinning systems can also enhance ductility.
The deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation provides CrCoNi with greater strength without sacrificing plastic deformation relative to CrMnFeCoNi.
The relevant initial materials, including CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi, can be prepared as single-phase fcc solid solutions.
CrCoNi is a Mn-depleted derivative of equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn-depleted alloys will develop a higher deformation-twin density than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
CrCoNi will develop a greater measurable hcp fraction during deformation than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn-depleted alloys will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn-depleted alloys will show an improved balance of strength and ductility relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Extreme grain refinement, secondary-phase formation, or sufficiently large compositional changes may replace the proposed mechanism with different deformation modes.
Processing-induced microstructural variation can affect the operative deformation mechanisms and mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The investigation is presented as a controlled variation of Mn, but replacing equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi with equiatomic CrCoNi removes Fe as well as Mn and changes the atomic fractions of Cr, Co, and Ni from 20% to about 33.3%. This comparison therefore cannot isolate Mn effects by itself.
The boundary limits the hypothesis to moderate Mn reduction, whereas the main example, CrCoNi, entails complete Mn removal and simultaneous Fe removal.
